artifact: POST-17.10 Step 10.6 (G7) — bounded provider rate-limit retry
head: b677654
verdict: G7 OPEN — PROVIDER BLOCKER (real-browser retry engagement unproven)

defects_found_and_fixed.defect: ReasoningError carried no Retry-After, so the provider's own published back-off was known only as text inside the error message.
defects_found_and_fixed.fix: Added a `retry_after` field populated verbatim from the upstream response header at the three 429 sites.
defects_found_and_fixed.classification_changed: none — retryable is still decided by the pre-existing sites; a rate limit remains non-retryable at the backend layer.

defects_found_and_fixed.defect: When the primary was rate-limited and the fallback then failed, the route reported `error_kind: fallback_err.kind` and a hardcoded `retryable: False`. The primary's rate limit survived only inside a human-readable `reason` string, where no client parses it.
defects_found_and_fixed.fix: Report `error_kind: rate_limit` and `retryable: true` truthfully, and relay the provider's Retry-After header — but ONLY when the provider actually emitted one. Absent header keeps the previous behaviour exactly.
defects_found_and_fixed.proved: Live probe: status=503, retry-after='4', kind='rate_limit', retryable=True.

defects_found_and_fixed.defect: Retry-After is NOT a CORS-safelisted response header. The extension's cross-origin fetch could not read it, so retryAfterMs was always undefined and the step correctly failed closed. This is why D2 appeared to have no effect in a real browser despite working in isolation.
defects_found_and_fixed.security: Exposes a timing header only. Access-Control-Allow-Credentials stays False and the origin regex stays localhost-only, so the local boundary is unchanged.

production_files_changed: extension/src/agent/goalVerifier.ts (from the immediately preceding G7 GoalVerifier task)

extension_change.change: parseError now takes the locally-parsed, clamped retryAfterMs; the final rate_limit guard sets `retryable = typeof retryAfterMs === 'number'`.
extension_change.note: agentLoop.ts needed NO change: requestActionWithBoundedRetry already reads retryAfterMs, clamps with Math.min(hint, 30_000) and bounds attempts by providerRetries.

tests.added: tests/step10_6_providerRateLimitRetry.test.ts — 12 tests covering all 10 required cases plus a clamp control and a no-duplicate-dispatch control. No real waiting: fake timers drive the Retry-After wait.

killed: R8 treat a failed retry as success

equivalent.proof: attempts are already bounded by `for (let attempt = 0; attempt <= this.providerRetries; attempt++)`; the inner `attempt >= this.providerRetries` break is redundant defence-in-depth and cannot change behaviour.
parseRetryAfter already clamps to MAX_HONOURED_RETRY_AFTER_MS, which IS 30000 — the identical bound. The loop-side Math.min(hint, 30_000) can never fire.

mutation.prior_matrices: Step 10.4 18/1/0 unchanged; Step 10.6 GoalVerifier 9 KILLED unchanged.

security_audit.m5_privacy_firewall: unchanged; the retry happens before any BrowserAction exists
security_audit.fail_closed: a rate limit with no valid Retry-After is still non-retryable with zero retries
security_audit.no_duplicate_side_effects: PROVEN by test: N provider failures produce zero browser dispatches, because a provider failure returns no BrowserAction to dispatch
security_audit.no_new_pii_egress: no new telemetry or payload fields; Retry-After is a timing header carrying no context, PII or gate decision

real_chrome_execution.runs_6_7_8: all identical: FAILED at step 3, 5 provider requests, statuses [200,200,200,200,503], final URL /search.html
real_chrome_execution.destinationVerifier: UNKNOWN on the search page (correct: the page is unclassified, so it can neither confirm nor deny)
real_chrome_execution.label: PROVEN_REAL for every stage up to form completion; NOT_REACHED for DestinationVerifier MATCH, subgoal completion, planner progression and GoalVerifier SUCCESS

remaining_blocker: The real-browser retry engagement is unproven. Each layer is individually proven: the backend emits status=503 + Retry-After + kind=rate_limit + retryable=true; the CORS layer exposes the header; the built extension bundle contains the new classification rule (`kind==='rate_limit' && (retryable = typeof retryAfterMs === 'number')`); and the loop already bounds and honours retryAfterMs. Ruled out so far: missing bundle rebuild (verified in dist), duplicate chunk breaking `instanceof ProviderError` (only one chunk defines both), and a stale backend process (confirmed the live process emits the new header). The next diagnostic is to instrument the service worker's parseError result (kind, retryable, retryAfterMs) during a real run.
